title: The Recipe Book (Wilma McIvor)
style: folk country acoustic guitar warm female vocal 98bpm brushed drums gentle storytelling intimate family Perth recipe cooking memory seasons
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The recipe book is held together by a rubber band and intention
Its pages are splattered with the evidence of every mention
Of a meal that was good enough to make again someday
The recipe book is the family's food autobiography in disarray

[Pre-Chorus]
I have three recipe books and the one I use is not actually a book
It's a collection of cards and clippings and whatever it took

[Chorus]
The recipe book knows something I don't know
It knows the meals behind the memories and how they flow
The recipe book has a stain on the page for the Christmas cake
That marks the December of the year it was too good to take
The gardens still growing

[Verse 2]
My mother's handwriting is on one of the cards — her biscuit recipe
A small yellowed card that I have never once not followed precisely
Because the biscuits taste of her and that's the point
The recipe book is the genealogy of every joint

[Bridge]
Pete doesn't cook but he eats everything presented to him fully
Corey makes one thing and it's extraordinary duly
Joel cooks quietly and well and says nothing about the result
The boys are in the recipe book in their own type of adult

[Outro]
Recipe book knows every meal ever made… the pages know…
The gardens still growing
